numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With missing values (NaN) present in X, DecisionTreeRegressor sometimes builds a tree with fewer leaves than expected (only one split is made, giving a single leaf of the other side); the impurity is reported as [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] instead of [0.25 0. 0.]; in the reproducer about half of 1000 fits gave 1 leaf (bincount [0 ~500 ~500]) instead of always 2 leaves. Cause: the last non-missing sample was not partitioned correctly when a different feature was examined first.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: All trees should have two leaves (tree.tree_.n_leaves == 2) and the impurity should be [0.25 0. 0.], i.e. the impurity decrease is computed correctly regardless of missing values.
trigger_conditions: X contains missing values (NaN), created here by X[X==0] = np.nan
the tree splitter first examines a different feature before the feature with missing values (order-dependent, roughly half of fits)
min_impurity_decrease=0.25 with max_depth=1 in the reproducer
random_state varies between fits (e.g. i=2 is a broken random state in the PR example)

input_output_examples.input: X = np.vstack([[0,0,0,0,1,2,3,4],[1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2]]).swapaxes(0,1).astype(float); y=[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]; X[X==0]=np.nan; DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, min_impurity_decrease=0.25).fit(X, y) repeated 1000 times
input_output_examples.buggy_output: tree.tree_.n_leaves is 1 in roughly 500 of 1000 fits; np.bincount(n_leaves_w_missing) prints approximately [0 500 500]
input_output_examples.expected_output: tree.tree_.n_leaves == 2 for every fit; bincount approximately [0 0 1000]

input_output_examples.input: same X with NaNs, y=[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1], DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i, min_impurity_decrease=0.002).fit(X, y) for i in range(50), reading tree.tree_.impurity

oracle_clues: bincount of n_leaves over 1000 fits should not show 1-leaf trees
non-regression test repeatedly fits (about ten to twenty trees) and checks computed impurity

category_specific_evidence: Issue #32178: with missing values in X, DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, min_impurity_decrease=0.25) yields a tree with two leaves in all 1000 fits without NaNs, but with NaNs the leaf count is about 500 one-leaf and about 500 two-leaf trees (np.bincount prints [0 ~500 ~500]), indicating the impurity decrease is miscomputed.

Expected impurity for the regression case is [0.25, 0.0, 0.0] (root impurity 0.25, two pure leaves), per the added non-regression test assert_array_equal(tree.tree_.impurity, np.array([0.25, 0.0, 0.0])).
Broken case reported in PR #32351: impurity is [0.25, 0.1875, 0.1875] instead of [0.25, 0.0, 0.0] for a random_state that triggers the bug (i=2).

Root cause per commit: partitioning with missing values did not examine one more value, so the last non-missing sample was not partitioned correctly (fix: examine one more value; off-by-one in start/end positions).
Non-regression test runs 20 trees with random_state=i so both feature orders are tried, since the bug occurs in roughly 50% of fits.
reproduction_risks: Results are stochastic across random_state; reproduction should loop over many fits (e.g., 1000 or at least 20) rather than a single fit.
The reproducer uses X[X == 0] = np.nan, so the zeros in the first feature become missing; keep the same construction to match the expected impurity values.
The exact bincount counts (~500 each) are approximate and should not be used as strict equality targets.
PR #32351 snippet uses min_impurity_decrease=0.002 in one variant, differing from the issue's 0.25 setting.
